problem_text:
A network of 11 research stations requires a maintenance team to perform a sequential inspection tour.  
Station Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (188,110)  
Station Beta: Positioned at grid reference (148,116)  
Station Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (125,65)  
Station Delta: Positioned at grid reference (180,121)  
Station Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (55,86)  
Station Zeta: Positioned at grid reference (68,10)  
Station Eta: Positioned at grid reference (11,13)  
Station Theta: Positioned at grid reference (41,89)  
Station Iota: Positioned at grid reference (0,74)  
Station Kappa: Positioned at grid reference (167,1)  
Station Lambda: Positioned at grid reference (35,16)  

The travel distances between stations, measured in kilometers, are as follows:  
Alpha to Gamma: 77.4 km

Theta to Kappa: 153.7 km  
Theta to Lambda: 73.2 km  
Iota to Kappa: 182.3 km  
Iota to Lambda: 67.7 km  
Kappa to Lambda: 132.8 km  

Due to a permanent obstruction, no direct route exists between Station Alpha and Station Beta.  
Furthermore, exactly one of the following two connections must be part of the inspection circuit: the link between Station Beta and Station Gamma, or the link between Station Gamma and Station Delta.  

The objective is to determine the shortest possible closed-circuit route that visits each station precisely once and returns to the origin station.
